text: It is knowledge, more than quick, flashy parts, that makes a man of business. A man who is master of his matter, twill, with inferior parts, be too hard in parliament, and indeed anywhere else, for a man of-better parts, who knows his subject but superficially: and if to his knowledge he joins eloquence and elocution, he must necessarily soon be at the head of that assembly; but without those two, no knowledge is sufficient.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXXVIII, to his son, London, January 21, Old Style. 1751
